rules.title: Discord webhook endpoint
rules.summary: A hard-coded Discord webhook can be used to send collected data out of the repository.
rules.recommendation: Check who owns the webhook, what data reaches it, and whether the endpoint is expected. Revoke any exposed webhook token.
rules.behavior: If executed along a data-collection path, the code could transmit information to a Discord webhook. The URL by itself does not prove any data was sent.
rules.install_effect: This URL alone does not execute at install. Data is sent only if surrounding code posts to it during setup or later use.

rules.title: Telegram bot API endpoint
rules.summary: A Telegram bot endpoint can be used as a covert channel for sending data or files.
rules.recommendation: Trace the data passed to this request and verify that the bot and recipient are authorized.
rules.behavior: If the request is reached, the code could send text or files to a Telegram bot/chat controlled by whoever owns the bot token.
rules.install_effect: This endpoint alone does not execute at install. Data is sent only if surrounding code calls it during setup or later use.

rules.title: Cryptomining indicator
rules.summary: A mining protocol, miner name, or mining algorithm is referenced.
rules.recommendation: Inspect the surrounding code for unauthorized mining, pool connections, and resource use.
rules.behavior: If run, a miner may consume CPU/GPU resources to mine cryptocurrency for a configured pool. Startup persistence would make it run again later.
rules.install_effect: Mining does not necessarily start when a package is installed. Check for an install hook, autorun entry, or task that launches the miner.

rules.title: Encoded PowerShell command
rules.summary: PowerShell is launched with a long encoded command, a technique that can conceal behavior.
rules.recommendation: Do not execute it. Decode and review the command in an isolated, offline analysis environment.
rules.behavior: The encoded command may hide PowerShell behavior; its actual actions cannot be inferred from the launch flag alone.
rules.install_effect: It runs during setup only if an installer or package hook launches this command; the encoded flag alone does not show when it runs.

rules.title: Download followed by execution
rules.summary: A network download appears connected to a command interpreter or dynamic execution.
rules.recommendation: Follow the downloaded content and verify its source and integrity before allowing any execution.
rules.behavior: If the chain runs, it may fetch code from a remote server and execute the response. The behavior can change when the remote content changes.
rules.install_effect: If a setup script invokes this chain, remote code may run during installation or later; the remote response can change.

rules.title: Obfuscated content passed to an execution function
rules.summary: Base64-decoded or browser-decoded text is near a dynamic execution call.
rules.recommendation: Treat the decoded content as untrusted and inspect it without running it.
rules.behavior: The code may decode hidden content and pass it to a dynamic execution function in the current process.
rules.install_effect: The payload executes only when that code path is invoked. Check whether setup or startup calls it.

rules.title: PHP web-shell pattern
rules.summary: Request-controlled input appears to reach a PHP execution primitive or encoded payload.
rules.recommendation: Do not expose this file to a web server. Review the full request-to-execution path and remove unauthorized access.
rules.behavior: If exposed through a web server, request-controlled input could reach a command or code execution primitive with the web-server account's permissions.
rules.install_effect: A web server must deploy and expose the PHP route; merely downloading the file does not execute it.

rules.title: Process injection API
rules.summary: A Windows API commonly associated with writing into or starting code inside another process is present.
rules.recommendation: Confirm this is required, authorized software behavior; inspect surrounding code and its origin carefully.
rules.behavior: If reached, these APIs can write or start code inside another process, potentially altering or hiding process behavior.
rules.install_effect: These APIs run only if the process reaches them with suitable permissions; their presence does not prove execution at install.

rules.title: Keyboard capture hook
rules.summary: A keyboard capture API or keylogger marker is present.
rules.recommendation: Verify that keystrokes are not recorded or transmitted without the user's informed consent.
rules.behavior: If active, the hook may observe keyboard input; surrounding code determines whether it records or transmits keystrokes.
rules.install_effect: Keystrokes are captured only if the hook is activated. Check whether the app starts automatically and sends captured input.

rules.title: Browser credential-store access
rules.summary: A browser password or cookie database path is referenced.
rules.recommendation: Check whether the file is being accessed for a legitimate migration or backup, and whether its contents leave the machine.
rules.behavior: The program may read browser credential databases, which can contain passwords, cookies, or login metadata.
rules.install_effect: Access depends on code running under a user account; it may occur during setup or later, but this path alone does not show timing.

rules.title: Discord local-token storage reference
rules.summary: Discord client token-storage locations are referenced.
rules.recommendation: Inspect for token harvesting and outbound transfer; rotate credentials if a token may have been exposed.
rules.behavior: The program may inspect Discord's local token storage; a stolen token could allow account access until revoked.
rules.install_effect: Access depends on code running under a user account; check whether setup or a startup task calls it.

rules.title: Wallet recovery-secret handling
rules.summary: Wallet recovery phrases or private keys appear near transfer or collection logic.
rules.recommendation: Never enter a real recovery phrase. Verify the code's purpose and assume any exposed secret is compromised.
rules.behavior: If used to collect or transmit a recovery phrase/private key, the wallet could be emptied by whoever receives it.
rules.install_effect: A wallet can be affected only if code obtains a real secret and transfers or misuses it; the match does not prove installation behavior.

rules.title: Reverse-shell command pattern
rules.summary: A shell or socket appears configured to call back to a remote host.
rules.recommendation: Do not run the file. Confirm whether remote command access is intentional and restrict network exposure.
rules.behavior: If run and reachable, the process may connect outward and provide a remote operator with command access.
rules.install_effect: A connection requires this code to run and network access to be available; the indicator alone does not prove an automatic install action.

rules.title: Windows autorun or scheduled-task persistence
rules.summary: A registry autorun location, Startup folder, or scheduled-task creation command is referenced.
rules.recommendation: Check what is being made persistent, whether the user is informed, and how it can be removed.
rules.behavior: If the referenced command writes an autorun or task entry, it may launch again at login or on a schedule, including after reboot.
rules.install_effect: If the referenced entry is created, it can make a payload start again at login or on a schedule.

rules.title: Hidden PowerShell window
rules.summary: PowerShell is started with its window hidden, which can conceal activity from the user.
rules.recommendation: Inspect the command and its parent process; legitimate administration tools should document this behavior.
rules.behavior: The PowerShell window may be hidden from the interactive user; this flag alone does not reveal the command's effect.
rules.install_effect: An installer can launch hidden PowerShell, but this match alone does not prove the command is part of setup.

rules.title: Destructive or shadow-copy deletion command
rules.summary: A command can remove recovery data or recursively delete files.
rules.recommendation: Confirm this destructive operation is explicitly intended and protected by backups and authorization.
rules.behavior: If executed with sufficient permissions, this command may delete files or recovery snapshots and cause data loss.
rules.install_effect: If a setup script invokes this command, it may delete files or recovery data. Never test it against real data.

rules.title: Package install lifecycle hook
rules.summary: A package lifecycle script runs automatically during installation; this is common but deserves review.
rules.recommendation: Inspect the exact command and any files or network locations it invokes before installing the package.
rules.behavior: Package managers run lifecycle commands during installation, so the command may execute before the package is used.
rules.install_effect: Package managers run these lifecycle scripts during installation; inspect each command and any scripts it calls.
